paragraphs: § The Story and Song of Salvation
God spoke to Moses: "Tell the Israelites to turn around and camp at Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Camp by the sea, opposite Baal Zephon."

"Pharaoh will think, 'The Israelites are lost — they're confused. The wilderness has closed in on them.' Then I'll make Pharaoh stubborn again and he'll chase after them. And I'll use Pharaoh and his army to put my Glory on display. Then the Egyptians will realize that I am God." And that's what happened.

When the king of Egypt was told the people were gone, he and his servants changed their minds. They said, "What have we done, letting Israel — our slave labor — go free?" So he had his chariots harnessed and gathered his army. He took six hundred of his best chariots, with the rest of Egypt's chariots and their drivers coming along.

God made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, stubborn — determined to chase the Israelites as they walked out on him without even looking back. The Egyptians chased them and caught up with them where they'd camped by the sea — all of Pharaoh's horse-drawn chariots and riders, all his foot soldiers, there at Pi Hahiroth opposite Baal Zephon.

As Pharaoh got closer, the Israelites looked up and saw them — Egyptians! Coming at them! They were terrified. They cried out in terror to God. They told Moses, "Weren't there enough cemeteries in Egypt that you had to drag us out here into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us, bringing us out of Egypt? Didn't we tell you back in Egypt this would happen? Didn't we say, 'Leave us alone in Egypt — we're better off as slaves in Egypt than as corpses in the wilderness'?"
Moses spoke to the people: "Don't be afraid. Stand firm and watch God do his saving work for you today. Take a good look at the Egyptians today — you're never going to see them again."
"God will fight the battle for you. And you? Keep your mouths shut!"

God said to Moses: "Why are you crying out to me? Talk to the Israelites. Order them to get moving. Hold your staff high and stretch your hand out over the sea: Split the sea! The Israelites will walk through the sea on dry ground."

"Meanwhile, I'll make sure the Egyptians keep up their stubborn chase — I'll use Pharaoh and his whole army, his chariots and horsemen, to put my Glory on display, so the Egyptians will realize that I am God."

The angel of God that had been leading Israel's camp now shifted and got behind them. And the Pillar of Cloud that had been in front also shifted to the rear. The Cloud stood between Egypt's camp and Israel's camp. The Cloud wrapped one camp in darkness and flooded the other with light. The two camps didn't come near each other all night.
Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and God — with a powerful east wind blowing all night long — pushed the sea back. He made the sea dry ground. The waters split.

The Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground, the waters like a wall to their right and to their left. The Egyptians came after them in full pursuit — every horse, chariot, and driver of Pharaoh racing into the middle of the sea. It was now the morning watch. God looked down from the Pillar of Fire and Cloud on the Egyptian army and threw them into a panic. He jammed the wheels of their chariots — they were stuck in the mud. The Egyptians said, "Run from Israel! God is fighting for them and against Egypt!"
God said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, and the waters will come back over the Egyptians — over their chariots, over their horsemen."

Moses stretched his hand out over the sea: as day broke and the Egyptians were running, the sea returned to its place as before. God dumped the Egyptians into the middle of the sea. The waters came back, drowning Pharaoh's chariots and riders — the whole army that had chased Israel into the sea. Not one of them survived.

But the Israelites walked right through the middle of the sea on dry ground, the waters forming a wall to the right and to the left. God rescued Israel that day from the Egyptians' grip. And Israel looked at the Egyptian dead, washed up on the seashore, and realized the tremendous power God had unleashed against the Egyptians. The people stood in reverent awe before God and trusted in God and his servant Moses.
title: The Red Sea
